root_cause.text: The BCM2835 power-domain driver’s `bcm2835_asb_control()` used an overly short 1 µs polling timeout for the ASB bridge ACK handshake, so under heavy load on BCM2711 the V3D master ASB could fail to acknowledge power-state changes and leave the device partially powered off.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces the open-coded `ktime_get_ns()`/`cpu_relax()` loop in `drivers/pmdomain/bcm/bcm2835-power.c` with `readl_poll_timeout_atomic()` and increases the timeout from `1000` ns to `5` µs, while the commit message says the handshake “intermittently fails for V3D's master ASB on BCM2711” because “the timeout is insufficient in some scenarios,” causing “Failed to disable ASB master for v3d” and broken power-off state.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the iopoll helper header so the driver can use kernel I/O polling APIs.
intent_record.what: A new header include, <linux/iopoll.h>, was added alongside the existing Linux kernel includes.
intent_record.how: This makes the iopoll helper APIs available to the translation unit, allowing the code to use polling helpers for repeated I/O register reads with timeout handling at compile time.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an unused local variable from bcm2835_asb_control().
intent_record.what: A local variable declaration `u64 start;` was removed from the `bcm2835_asb_control()` function, while the rest of the function signature and body shown in the hunk remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: This change has no runtime behavioral effect in the shown code; it only eliminates an unused variable from the function, avoiding a compiler warning and keeping the implementation cleaner.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an unnecessary timestamp capture from the ASB control path.
intent_record.what: The line assigning `start = ktime_get_ns();` was removed from `bcm2835_asb_control()` before the code that enables or disables the module's async AXI bridges.
intent_record.how: This change stops recording a timestamp at that point in the function, so any timing measurement or elapsed-time logic that depended on `start` being set there will no longer occur from this location.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace the manual register polling loop with `readl_poll_timeout_atomic()` for cleaner timeout-based ACK waiting.
intent_record.what: The busy-wait loop that repeatedly read `base + reg`, called `cpu_relax()`, and manually checked a 1000 ns timeout was replaced with a single `readl_poll_timeout_atomic()` call that polls the register until `!!(val & ASB_ACK) != enable`, with a 0-delay and 5 timeout parameter, returning `-ETIMEDOUT` on failure.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now uses the kernel polling helper to wait for the ASB acknowledgment bit to reach the desired state instead of spinning in an explicit loop. This changes the timeout handling to be delegated to the helper and preserves the same overall behavior of failing with `-ETIMEDOUT` if the register does not respond in time.

candidates.rationale: This is the timeout check enforcing only a 1 microsecond polling window for the ASB ACK handshake. The root cause says the timeout was too short, causing ACK failures under load and leaving the device partially powered off.

This is the polling loop that waits for the ASB bridge ACK bit to change state. Combined with the too-short timeout, it directly implements the fragile handshake that could fail on BCM2711 under heavy load.
This shows the busy-wait polling behavior used during the ACK handshake. The issue is not this line alone, but it is part of the manual loop that relied on an overly short timeout.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the timeout condition enforcing only a 1 microsecond polling window for the ASB ACK handshake. The root cause states the ACK wait timeout was too short, so this statement directly caused premature failure under load.

This is part of the manual polling loop used while waiting for the ASB ACK handshake. It contributes to the timeout-based busy wait that was too short for reliable operation under heavy load.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet shows the exact ASB polling logic in `bcm2835_asb_control()`. The vulnerable/refactored bug was that the loop only checked `while (readl(base + reg) & ASB_ACK)` and therefore did not distinguish enable vs disable semantics. The patch changes this to `while (!!(readl(base + reg) & ASB_ACK) == enable)`, which is the fix described in the commit message: "we need to check if !!(readl(base + reg) & ASB_ACK) == enable, not just check if (readl(base + reg) & ASB_ACK) == true." This function body is sufficient to determine the presence of the buggy construct in the pre-fix form and that the shown code already contains the fix. The 1 us timeout (`if (ktime_get_ns() - start >= 1000)`) is present, but the issue here is the incorrect ACK condition, and the corrected equality check is already applied.
